slots.hypothesis: The core K is head +0.67 itself: the 60-day standard deviation of the daily 1-minute-return skewness, with the long book buying the most stable shapes. It is the only head off the back-adjusted price axis, the only one never dissected, and has the lowest valid/train ratio (1.36). The window evidence (10/30/60 -> +0.03/+0.12/+0.67) says it is a slow trait. K mixes real shape variation with the estimator's own sampling noise (fat tails, tick discreteness). The periphery has four parts, all new since K had none: (1) VOV scale normalization, div(K, 60-day mean or median |skew|), after Baltussen et al. 2018; (2) normalization by the square root of mean kurtosis, which also tests whether K only reads 'no jump minutes'; (3) K as a measurement-quality gate: cs_first_low20 / cs_last_high20 pools ranked inside by low realized skew (the Amaya direction; Amaya et al. use 5-minute data and exclude low prices for the same reason) or by low normalized MAX (Bali et al.); (4) control seeds that rank K within deciles of nominal price and of zero-return-minute share. No price, size or amount levels, no convex transforms. OOS case: slow variable, low turnover, a cross-market VOV effect, and the head does not depend on the 2022-23 style. 12 seeds.

Closing-session price pressure reverses. Head +0.58 buys stocks whose volume comes early in the day (-2*day_centroid(sqrt(Volume)), enrichment +0.93, p 0.007). Non-informational pressure from passive/ETF and institutional rebalancing concentrates in the last 30 minutes and the closing auction (Bogousslavsky-Muravyev), as do closing-price manipulation and window dressing (Hillion-Suominen 2004, Comerton-Forde-Putnins 2011, Carhart et al. 2002). Flow-driven pressure reverts over weeks (Coval-Stafford 2007). Single-day deviations mostly revert overnight, before the label's 09:31-09:45 VWAP entry, so the seeds use only 10-60 day aggregates. Operators: close vs the daily VWAP log(div(day_last(Close), day_wmean(Vwap, Amt))), as mean, median, t-stat and intraday-vol-standardized versions; the last-30-minute return via in_delay(Close, 30); the last-30-minute turnover share via is_gt(in_index(Amt), 0.875), where 0.875 is the bar 211-240 boundary; that share times the close deviation; and the turnover centroid with its abnormal shift. Seeds are negated, so the long book holds names pushed down at the close. The inputs differ from every head (only +0.58 has the centroid), there are no level or convex transforms, and closing-auction rules have been unchanged in both exchanges since 2018-08. 13 seeds.

I wrote the round-2 plan for seed 804 and appended a 「第 2 轮」 section to the notebook. The final run of `c06_check.py 804 2` returned ADMISSIBLE (exit code 0).

**Slot a (E):** the core is head +0.67, `cross_stddev(day_skew(Ret), 60)`, used whole. It is the only clean head off the back-adjusted price axis and the only one never dissected. It also has the best valid/train ratio. It has no periphery yet, so every seed's periphery is new:
- dividing by the 60-day mean or median of |skew| (the VOV form from Baltussen et al. 2018);
- dividing by the square root of mean kurtosis, which tests whether the head only reads minutes without jumps;
- using K as a measurement-quality pool, ranked inside by low skew (the Amaya direction) or low normalized MAX (Bali et al.);
- two control seeds that rank K within deciles of nominal price and of zero-return-minute share.
There are 12 seeds.

**Slot b (N):** the idea is that pressure at the close reverses. It comes from the volume-centroid term in head +0.58, with the mechanism from the literature on fund-flow pressure and closing-price manipulation (Coval-Stafford, Bogousslavsky-Muravyev, Comerton-Forde-Putniņš, Hillion-Suominen, Carhart et al.). The seeds measure:
- the close relative to the day's VWAP;
- the return over the last 30 minutes;
- the share of turnover in the last 30 minutes;
- the volume centroid.
All seeds use 10–60 day aggregates, because single-day deviations revert before the label's entry. There are 13 seeds.

**R (4 groups, 5 variants):**
- R1 drops the `ts_mean(·, 20)` around the filter output used as the block variable in head +1.56; the dissection already measured this at +1.66.
- R2 makes the same cut in head +1.22, already measured at +1.33.
- R3 transfers the same cut to head +0.79, untested; its replacement threshold is +0.89.
- R4 splits the block variable in head +0.88 into log nominal price and the log cumulative adjustment factor. The previous auditor suggested this. Both halves need +0.98.

**Risks:**
- The correlation of K with the controls has never been computed. I estimate about a 75% chance it passes the core check (|ρ| < 0.5).
- The two bucket-control seeds in slot a will probably be struck by the table (|ρ| ≥ 0.7 with head +0.67).
- The auditor may score R4 as testing a new signal rather than removing a bad part, and delete the group.
